==English== ===Alternative forms=== * {{alter|en|favorable||US}} ===Etymology=== From {{inh|en|enm|favourable}}, from {{der|en|fro|favorable}}, from {{der|en|la|favōrābilis}}, from {{m|la|favor}}. {{surf|en|favour|-able}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈfeɪv(ə)ɹəbəl/}} * {{audio|en|En-us-favorable.ogg|a=US}} ===Adjective=== {{en-adj}} {{lb|en|British spelling}} # Apt to win [[favour]]; [[pleasing]]. #: {{syn|en|good|pleasing}} #: {{ant|en|bad|displeasing|unfavorable}} #: {{ux|en|The candidate wearing the business suit made a '''favourable''' impression.}} # Expressing or indicating [[favour]] or [[goodwill]]; [[approving]], [[encouraging]]. #: {{syn|en|approving|encouraging|positive}} #: {{ant|en|disapproving|discouraging|negative|unfavourable}} #: {{ux|en|The proposal has received many '''favourable''' comments.}} # {{U|useful}} or [[helpful]]. #: {{syn|en|advantageous|helpful|useful|propitious}} #: {{ant|en|unfavourable|unhelpful}} #: {{ux|en|We made quick progress, due to '''favourable''' winds.}} #* {{RQ:Tennyson In Memoriam|IX||So draw him home to those that mourn
⁠In vain; a '''favourable''' speed
⁠Ruffle thy mirror’d mast, and lead
Thro’ prosperous floods his holy urn.}} #* {{RQ:Guardian|date=August 1 2012|author=Peter Walker; Haroon Siddique|url=http://www.guardian.co.uk/sport/2012/aug/01/london-2012-badminton-disqualified-olympics|title=Eight Olympic badminton players disqualified for 'throwing games' |passage=Four pairs of women's doubles badminton players, including the Chinese top seeds, have been ejected from the Olympic tournament for trying to throw matches in an effort to secure a more '''favourable''' quarter-final draw.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240801052011/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2012/aug/01/london-2012-badminton-disqualified-olympics}} # {{U|convenient}} or at a [[suitable]] [[time]]; [[opportune]]. #: {{syn|en|convenient|good|handy|opportune|suitable}} #: {{ant|en|bad|inconvenient|inopportune|unfavourable|unsuitable}} #: {{ux|en|The rain stopped at a '''favourable''' time for our tennis match.}} # [[auspicious|Auspicious]] or [[lucky]]. #: {{syn|en|auspicious|fortunate|lucky}} #: {{ant|en|inauspicious|unfavourable|unlucky}} #: {{ux|en|She says that she was born under a '''favourable''' star.}} ====Derived terms==== {{col|en|disfavourable |favourableness |unfavourable }} ====Related terms==== {{col4|en |favour |favourably |favourite }} ====Translations==== {{trans-top|pleasing}} * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Czech: * Danish: * Esperanto: * Etruscan: * Finnish: * French: * Galician: * Georgian: * German: * Hebrew: * Hindi: * Irish: * Italian: * Latin: * Māori: * Middle English: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|благоприя́тный}}, {{t+|ru|прия́тный}} * Ukrainian: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|expressing or indicating favour or goodwill}} * German: * Greek: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|useful}} * Armenian: * Azerbaijani: * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Czech: * Danish: * Finnish: * French: * Galician: * Georgian: * German: * Greek: * Hindi: * Hungarian: * Italian: * Māori: * Middle English: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|благоприя́тный}}, {{t+|ru|благоприя́тствующий}} * Ukrainian: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|opportune}} * Armenian: * Azerbaijani: * Bulgarian: * Chinese: * Danish: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * French: * Galician: * Georgian: * German: * Italian: * Japanese: * Māori: * Norwegian: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Russian: {{t+|ru|благоприя́тный}}, {{t+|ru|удо́бный}}, {{t+|ru|подходя́щий}} * Spanish: * Telugu: * Ukrainian: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|auspicious}} * Catalan: * Danish: * Finnish: * French: * Galician: * Georgian: * German: * Italian: * Latin: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|благоприя́тный}} * Turkish: {{trans-bottom}} {{cln|en|3-syllable words}}
